instructions: Slice the sausage into 1-inch rounds. Halve the onion and slice it into half-moons. Cut the peppers into 1-inch pieces. Mince the garlic.
Heat a large, wide skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the olive oil and the sausage in a single layer. Cook for 5 minutes, turning once, until both sides are browned.
Transfer the sausage to a plate. Spoon all but about 1 tbsp of the fat out of the pan.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the onion, with 1/4 tsp salt. Cook over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until it starts to soften.
Add the peppers and cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Add the tomato paste, oregano and paprika. Stir for 1 minute, until the paste turns a shade darker.
Add the wine and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bubble for 2 minutes, until most of it has cooked off.

Add the canned tomatoes with their juice, 1/4 cup water and 1/2 tsp salt. Return the sausage and any juices from the plate. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook over medium-low heat for 9 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the sauce has thickened.
You're cooking the sausage to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and stir it in off the heat.
Serve with the crusty bread. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for anyone who wants heat.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Runs about 31 minutes, a touch over 30, because the sausage browns first and the peppers need a covered simmer. No version had 20 or more ratings (Real Greek Recipes has 4.75 from 16, Mia Kouppa 5 from 11, the other sites show none), so the lead is the best-read real version. Sources agree on browned sausage, onion and bell pepper, tomato, wine, oregano and a covered simmer; they differ on fresh against canned tomato, tomato paste, red against white wine and whether it's a 20 or 45 minute dish. I used canned tomato and a short simmer to keep it near 30 minutes, added paste fried until dark for depth, and moved the pepper flakes to the table.
